# tidycjk <img src="man/figures/logo.png" align="right" height="148" alt="tidycjk hex logo" />

<!-- badges: start -->
[![Lifecycle: stable](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-stable-brightgreen.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#stable)
[![CRAN status](https://www.r-pkg.org/badges/version/tidycjk)](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=tidycjk)
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/PursuitOfDataScience/tidycjk/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/PursuitOfDataScience/tidycjk/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

Tidy tools for Chinese, Japanese and Korean text. R's text tooling assumes
words are separated by whitespace; CJK writing does not oblige.

<img src="man/figures/hero-width.svg" width="100%" alt="Padding by character count leaves a CJK column ragged; padding by display width aligns it." />

## Installation

```r
install.packages("tidycjk")
```

## What you get

|  |  |
|---|---|
| **Detect** | `has_cjk()` · `cjk_script()` · `cjk_detect_language()` · `cjk_ratio()` |
| **Measure** | `cjk_width()` · `cjk_char_counts()` · `cjk_summary()` |
| **Lay out** | `cjk_pad()` · `cjk_truncate()` |
| **Normalise** | `to_halfwidth()` · `to_fullwidth()` |
| **Segment** | `cjk_tokens()` · `cjk_segment()` · `register_cjk_segmenter()` |

Every verb is vectorised and propagates `NA`. Three of them —
`cjk_summary()`, `cjk_char_counts()` and `cjk_tokens()` — also take
`(data, column)` and return a tibble straight into a
[dplyr](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=dplyr) pipeline.

## Which script, which language?

<img src="man/figures/fig-scripts.png" width="100%" alt="cjk_script and cjk_detect_language over five sample strings." />

```{r language}
library(tidycjk)

cjk_detect_language(c("こんにちは", "안녕하세요", "東京都"))
```

東京都 is Tokyo — Japanese — but it is written entirely in Han characters, and
nothing in the script separates it from Chinese. Anything that answers
`"chinese"` there is guessing. Ask for the guess explicitly if you want it:

```{r language-optin}
cjk_detect_language("東京都", han_only = "chinese")
```

## How much of this is CJK?

<img src="man/figures/fig-ratio.png" width="100%" alt="cjk_ratio over four sample strings, shown as filled bars." />

```{r summary}
posts <- data.frame(
  id = 1:3,
  text = c("我今天很開心", "hello 中文 world", "no CJK here")
)

cjk_summary(posts, text)
```

`prop_with_cjk` answers "how many of these rows are CJK at all"; `mean_ratio`
answers "how CJK are they".

## Width, not character count

<img src="man/figures/fig-width.png" width="100%" alt="nchar padding leaves the right edge ragged; cjk_pad aligns it." />

```{r width}
labels <- c("中文", "abcd", "日本語")

nchar(labels)      # all look comparable
cjk_width(labels)  # they are not

cat(paste0("|", cjk_pad(labels, 8), "|"), sep = "\n")
```

## Fullwidth and halfwidth

<img src="man/figures/fig-normalize.png" width="100%" alt="to_halfwidth narrows width forms and leaves everything else alone." />

The usual advice is `NFKC`, which fixes width and also rewrites ligatures,
Roman numerals and circled numbers. `to_halfwidth()` changes width and nothing
else.

```{r normalize}
as.numeric(to_halfwidth("１２３"))

nchar("ｶﾞ")                 # U+FF76 U+FF9E, two code points
to_halfwidth("ｶﾞ") == "ガ"   # composed into one
```

## Segmentation

Where a word ends is a fact about a language, not about Unicode, so no
dictionary is bundled and `engine` is required — quietly handing back character
tokens to someone who asked for words is the mistake this package exists to
avoid.

```{r segment}
cjk_segment("hello 中文 world", engine = "character")
```

`"character"` is the one engine needing no dictionary: one token per CJK
character, non-CJK runs split on whitespace. For real Chinese word
segmentation register [jiebaR](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=jiebaR)
(archived from CRAN 2025-05-01, so
`remotes::install_github("qinwf/jiebaR")`):

```r
register_cjk_segmenter("jiebar", function(x, ...) {
  worker <- jiebaR::worker(...)
  lapply(x, function(s) as.character(jiebaR::segment(s, worker)))
})

cjk_segment("我今天很開心", engine = "jiebar")
```

`cjk_blocks()` exports the block table the whole package is built on, so the
definition of "CJK" can be read rather than guessed at.

## Related work

| Need | Use |
|---|---|
| Display width, width-aware padding | [stringi](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=stringi) — `stri_width()` and `stri_pad()`, which `cjk_width()` and `cjk_pad()` wrap |
| Chinese segmentation | [jiebaR](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=jiebaR) — register it as a `tidycjk` engine |
| Pinyin | [pinyin](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=pinyin), [hanyupinyin](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=hanyupinyin) |
| Traditional/simplified | [tmcn](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=tmcn); [OpenCC](https://github.com/BYVoid/OpenCC) outside R |
| Japanese utilities | [zipangu](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=zipangu), [Nippon](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=Nippon) |
